purpose: Describe, as testable criteria, the release-lifecycle contract as implemented on branch codex/release-recovery (PR 101): run envelope, provider observation and evidence, the transition table, the provider port, protocol-level registry, tag and forge observation, retry and deadlines, validation before effects, canonical destinations, redaction, the workflow adapter policy, and the verification tiers that keep them honest.
scope: The implemented behavior of the release path in callisto-model, callisto-graph, callisto-cli, the release workflow, the setup-callisto installer and the provider contract tier. Every criterion cites its source file and the tests or policy self-test mutants that pin it. Provenance tags: [UR] owner requirement, [EC] existing contract already stated in docs/07-self-release-lifecycle.md or a sibling spec, [XC] external constraint from observed provider behavior, [JC] judgment call awaiting owner acceptance.
non_goals: Replacing the three superseded design drafts' proposals that were not implemented (an HTTP client crate for registry observation, in-process provider clients).
A data-driven [release] catalog for adopters other than Callisto; the target table stays Callisto-specific.
A workspace-hack crate, npm evidence beyond npm view, and exercising the Blocked and EffectFailedAndAbsent events outside tests.
Hosted CI results and a GitHub dry run of the workflow; both are pending and outside this spec's evidence.
The unpinned rust-cache action inside orin-dx/actions/setup-rust, the bot-PR check policy for the managed release PR, and token rotation; these need the owner.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: [EC] A run envelope (orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest; one run kind, no profile) is validated against the intent: schema, digest, manifest-digest presence (exactly when the intent declares artifact slots), orchestration revision equal to every slot's attestation workflow commit, and release-source revision equal to the intent's Git source each reject independently. An intent or envelope carrying a profile, or of another schema version, is rejected naming what was found. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs. Tests: envelope_rejects_each_cross_field_mismatch, intent_has_no_profile_and_rejects_one_on_the_wire, envelope_has_no_profile_and_other_schema_versions_name_the_found_version.

[EC] The envelope is held inside ReleaseExecutionStateV1, which lives in memory only: it is never persisted or loaded, every run (including a CI rerun) starts with every operation Pending, and execute has no state-file input. `callisto schema` publishes no release-state shape; the receipt's envelope is schema version 2 with no run kind. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs, crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs, crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/schema.rs. Tests: durable_release_wire_shapes_match_their_schema_version, p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt.

[EC] The receipt is built from the execution state alone (ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state): its run envelope plus the exact evidence each operation recorded on reaching Published or AlreadySatisfied. It makes no provider call, requires every operation to be terminal success, rejects a state bound to another intent, and rejects deserialized receipts with non-Exact or missing observations or an unknown schema. An artifact manifest whose source_commit differs from the intent's Git source, or whose attestation source is not the coordinator revision, is rejected. The manifest itself carries no signature; its integrity rests on the digest binding to the intent. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs, crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs. Tests: receipt_records_the_evidence_in_state_and_needs_every_operation_terminal, deserialized_receipt_rejects_nonexact_or_missing_observations, receipt_rejects_a_state_bound_to_another_intent, receipt_wire_rejects_unknown_schema, p11_receipt_is_bound_to_intent_and_provider_evidence, red_c6_manifest_with_forged_source_commit_is_rejected, artifact_manifest_rejects_attestation_source_that_is_not_the_coordinator_revision, artifact_manifest_requires_exact_slot_digest_and_source_binding.

[EC] A provider observation is exactly one of Absent, Exact, Conflict, Indeterminate. Exact carries typed per-role evidence (registry version with checksum and yanked flag, tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, asset size and sha256), and evidence that does not match the operation's role is rejected, including when the state would record it (E177). Conflict reasons and Indeterminate causes are closed enums. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs, crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs. Tests: observation_rejects_evidence_that_does_not_match_the_operation_role, apply_rejects_success_evidence_of_another_role.

[EC] An authentication, transport, rate-limit or unrecognised-answer failure is Indeterminate, never Conflict and never Absent; absence is proved only by a definite not-found answer. A registry observation may answer Absent only on cargo's exact "could not find `NAME@VERSION`" phrase or npm's E404; every other failure, including an unreachable registry, is transient Indeterminate. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/github.rs. Tests: a_plain_forbidden_answer_settles_immediately_rather_than_burning_the_attempts, a_persistent_server_error_exhausts_the_attempts_and_reports_its_status, an_unreachable_registry_is_indeterminate_and_never_absent, the_captured_network_failure_is_transient_not_absent, the_captured_absent_run_of_one_crate_does_not_answer_for_another, github_release_status_only_proves_absence_for_not_found, p09_indeterminate_forge_observation_fails_closed.

[EC] A single pure transition function is the only way an operation's state changes; the legal (state, event) edge set equals an explicit list, and no bounded event sequence reaches a success state without a legal edge. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release_transition.rs. Tests: every_state_event_pair_matches_the_explicit_allowed_list, no_bounded_event_sequence_reaches_success_without_a_legal_edge.

[EC] Attempting is reachable only through an absent proof minted from an observation; it is recorded only after an absent observation in the same run, so a failed pre-effect observation never strands an operation. Effects (publish, push, release create, asset upload) are never re-issued by the retry policy: a failed effect fails the run nonzero with no receipt and no dependent effect, and a rerun issues the effect again only if the provider then observes it Absent. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release_transition.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs. Tests: an_operation_can_never_be_marked_attempting_without_observing_absence, red_c7_pre_effect_observation_failure_does_not_wedge_rerun, failed_publish_fails_the_run_and_never_tags, p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt.

[EC] Every run adopts already-landed effects: exact success observed before an effect becomes AlreadySatisfied for every role (registry and platform versions, tags, forge releases, artifacts, forge publication) and is never issued again, and each adopted registry or platform version prints exactly one `warning: <package> <version> is already published; skipping` line. Published (this run's attempt landed) is distinct from AlreadySatisfied (it already existed). A Conflict observation fails closed with E167 and is never adopted. Source: crates/callisto-model/src/release_transition.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/mod.rs. Tests: p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt, a_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_with_a_receipt, p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed, a_release_already_published_with_every_asset_is_already_satisfied.

[EC] Rerunning a partially completed release (a CI "Re-run failed jobs" or a dispatch for the same release source) completes it: the rerun adopts every operation already exactly done, performs the rest in DAG order, and issues a receipt, with no flag or state from the earlier run. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs. Tests: p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt, newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source, a_rerun_over_a_half_filled_draft_uploads_the_rest_and_then_publishes.

[EC] A receipt is issued only when every operation is Published (confirmed by an Exact observation) or AlreadySatisfied, transitively through prerequisites; Attempting, failed, blocked, missing and indeterminate operations are non-success and block dependents. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs. Tests: quiescent_incomplete_state_is_never_successful, every_verified_terminal_success_allows_completion, reconciliation_requires_transitive_exact_successes, non_successful_or_attempting_prerequisites_never_make_dependents_eligible, direct_success_cannot_hide_an_unsatisfied_transitive_prerequisite.

[EC] The executor depends only on the ReleaseProviderSet port; an in-memory set drives the real executor, and an effect requires both an ApplyPermit and an AbsentProof obtainable only from an absent observation. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/mod.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs. Tests: the_release_executor_survives_every_enumerated_crash_and_provider_fault, an_operation_can_never_be_marked_attempting_without_observing_absence.

[EC] Provider capabilities are explicit: no production provider can publish without being observable, a publish-only role is refused, an ecosystem whose registry client cannot prove a version absent is refused at plan time, and an ecosystem with no adapter is Unsupported. A prepared operation carries only graph-private invocation data (package dir, tag, target, binding); the tag adapter accepts only the exact intended target and rejects a conflicting existing one. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/mod.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/mod.rs. Tests: no_production_provider_can_publish_without_being_observable, a_publish_only_role_is_refused_and_every_other_shape_is_allowed, cargo_and_npm_are_observable_and_pass_the_plan_time_gate, pypi_is_not_observable_and_is_refused_at_plan_time, an_ecosystem_with_no_registry_adapter_is_unsupported, prepared_capability_retains_exact_tag_and_registry_inputs, prepared_tag_adapter_accepts_only_the_exact_intended_target, prepared_tag_adapter_rejects_conflicting_existing_target.

[EC] A publish returns a post-effect observation, never the client's exit code: neither a zero exit nor a client's 'already exists'/'already uploaded' text satisfies an operation, and an unconfirmed publish reports its own error variant. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs. Tests: c5_already_uploaded_text_without_registry_observation_is_not_success, c5_already_exists_text_without_registry_observation_is_not_success, require_registry_confirmation_rejects_unconfirmed_publish_with_its_own_variant, require_registry_confirmation_accepts_a_confirmed_publish.

[XC] crates.io observation runs real `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY`: a version the registry serves is Exact (checksum None and yanked None, because `cargo info` reports neither), a version the registry does not serve and a crate it has never heard of are both Absent, and an unreachable registry index is Indeterminate, never Absent. A yanked version reads as Absent because `cargo info` cannot see yanks; that fails closed, since the following publish is refused by the registry and only an Exact observation may satisfy an operation. A workspace member of the same name whose on-disk version is unpublished is still Absent, because `--registry` is never omitted. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs. Tests: a_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact_with_no_checksum_or_yank_claim, a_version_the_registry_does_not_serve_is_absent, a_crate_the_registry_has_never_heard_of_is_absent, a_yanked_version_reads_as_absent_because_cargo_info_cannot_see_yanks, a_local_workspace_member_of_the_same_name_is_not_read_as_a_published_version, an_unreachable_registry_is_indeterminate_and_never_absent, the_captured_found_run_is_exact_for_the_version_it_names, the_captured_found_run_does_not_satisfy_another_version, the_captured_absent_unknown_and_yanked_runs_are_all_absent.

[XC] PyPI is not supported by durable release: pip cannot distinguish a missing project from an unreachable index, so a PyPI version can never be proved absent. A PyPI publish target is refused at plan time with ReleasePreconditionUnmet(ObservableRegistryClient) (E170), whose message names that reason and the way forward (publish outside durable release, or wait for a reliable observation), and no intent file is written. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs. Tests: pypi_is_not_observable_and_is_refused_at_plan_time, a_pypi_publish_target_is_refused_at_plan_time_because_pip_cannot_prove_absence.

[JC] Registry observation goes through the ecosystem package manager -- the same tool and configuration the publish effect uses, so registry resolution and authentication (private registries included) are the tool's job, not a credential-free reimplementation. cargo: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY` through the bounded CommandRunner at timeouts::REGISTRY_QUERY, run from the source workspace root so its .cargo/config.toml applies, with the logical cratesIo key mapped to cargo's built-in crates-io; `--registry` is never omitted. Classification: exit 0 plus a `version: VERSION` line is Exact (checksum None, yanked None), exit 101 plus "could not find `NAME@VERSION`" is Absent, everything else is transient Indeterminate under the retry policy. npm is unchanged (`npm view NAME@VERSION version --json`, E404 is Absent). PyPI is refused at plan time (AC-015). Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs. Tests: the_observation_argv_always_names_a_registry, red_d01_every_cargo_info_observation_names_a_registry_explicitly, the_captured_found_run_is_exact_for_the_version_it_names, the_captured_absent_unknown_and_yanked_runs_are_all_absent, the_captured_network_failure_is_transient_not_absent, the_captured_npm_view_runs_are_exact_and_absent, every_emitted_cargo_flag_exists_in_real_cargo_help, every_emitted_npm_flag_exists_in_real_npm_help.

[JC] One bounded retry policy wraps read-only observations: at most 5 attempts, exponential backoff 2s,4s,8s,16s, a server's Retry-After (delta-seconds or HTTP date) replaces the schedule and is clamped to 300s, HTTP 429/5xx and a rate-limited 403 are transient, a plain 403 settles immediately, a hard error is not retried, and exhaustion reports the last transient answer with no trailing sleep. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/http.rs. Tests: a_settled_first_attempt_never_sleeps, a_transient_answer_is_retried_on_the_exponential_schedule, exhausted_attempts_report_the_last_transient_answer_with_no_trailing_sleep, a_servers_retry_after_replaces_the_schedule_and_is_clamped_to_the_cap, a_hard_error_is_propagated_without_retrying, a_rate_limited_answer_is_retried_after_the_servers_own_delay_and_then_settles, a_plain_forbidden_response_is_not_a_rate_limit, retry_after_reads_both_delta_seconds_and_an_http_date, an_unreachable_registry_is_indeterminate_and_never_absent.

[JC] The post-publish confirmation observes registry operations with the lag-tolerant retry (Absent is transient there): a registry that serves the version only after a delay still yields a receipt, and one that never serves it yields none. The receipt is not re-observed after the effects, so once confirmation recorded Exact evidence a later registry read failure cannot fail the release. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs, crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs. Tests: a_lagging_registry_at_confirmation_still_yields_a_receipt, a_registry_read_failing_after_confirmation_cannot_cost_the_receipt, a_registry_that_never_serves_the_version_yields_no_receipt.

[JC] Every outbound command runs under a wall-clock deadline supplied by the run-with-timeout runner; a breach kills the process and returns CommandError::TimedOut. The per-command values live only in provider::policy::timeouts. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs, crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs. Tests: run_with_timeout_kills_slow_process_and_returns_timed_out.

[XC] Tag observation runs git ls-remote against the prepared remote endpoint for refs/tags/NAME and refs/tags/NAME^{}: an annotated tag resolves to its peeled commit, no output is Absent, a lightweight tag is Conflict(UnannotatedTag), a git failure is transient Indeterminate. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs. Tests: a_captured_annotated_tag_resolves_to_its_peeled_commit, a_captured_lightweight_tag_is_unannotated, captured_empty_output_is_an_absent_tag_and_garbled_output_is_not, red_p20_lightweight_preexisting_tag_reports_a_typed_conflict.

[EC] A local-only tag is pushed to the remote before the receipt, a conflicting local tag fails closed with no receipt, and the tag operation succeeds, and so reaches the receipt, only when the remote tag is observed at the intended commit. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs. Tests: red_d08_local_only_tag_is_pushed_to_the_remote_before_the_receipt, p10_conflicting_local_tag_fails_closed_and_issues_no_receipt.

[XC] The forge release is observed through gh api with no --repo flag and never by target_commitish (GitHub reports the default branch there); the tag operation, a DAG prerequisite, binds the release name to its commit. A draft is found by scanning the list endpoint page by page, bounded at 10 pages of 100. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/forge.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/github.rs. Tests: red_d02_release_runs_against_a_gh_that_rejects_unknown_api_flags, red_d03_normal_run_succeeds_when_forge_reports_default_branch_as_target, red_d03_rerun_succeeds_and_uploads_assets_when_forge_reports_default_branch, the_list_scan_pages_until_it_finds_the_draft, an_exhausted_bounded_scan_reports_absence_rather_than_paging_forever, a_draft_listed_on_the_second_page_is_found_and_never_recreated, the_captured_gh_output_parses_with_its_status_headers_and_body.

[JC] The GitHub Release is created as a draft, every asset is uploaded to the draft, and publication is a separate ForgePublish operation that depends on every upload; a release with no artifacts is still published, and a half-filled draft is completed then published. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/forge.rs. [EC] A release whose prerelease flag disagrees with the version is a Conflict with no effect issued; a remote asset of the same size but different sha256 is a Conflict; a published release missing an asset re-uploads only that asset. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/forge.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/artifact.rs. [UR,EC] Every execute input is validated before the first effect: orchestration revision syntax, release SHA (full, resolvable), artifact inputs and manifest, so a late failure cannot leave published effects without a receipt. Plan and execute resolve the same workspace root from a subdirectory. Source: crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs. [EC] `[release] forge-repository` is the destination authority: a `[release]` without it cannot derive a release (E198); legacy `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is migrated at load, a differing top-level value or any other profile name is rejected; plan rejects an artifact repository that differs from the git remote or the configured forge repository, and execute rejects an intent whose artifact repository is not the configured one. [JC] A source without a [release] section plans with zero artifact slots and prints a notice; a bare (ecosystem-unqualified) product package is rejected. Source: crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs. [EC] Each publish target binds its own registry key (no routing indirection); a configured key uses its `[registries]` entry and an unconfigured built-in key binds its built-in endpoint. GitHub repository identities are canonical: embedded whitespace, extra path parts and leading/trailing hyphens are rejected, and an invalid `forge-repository` fails config load. Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/binding.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs, crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs. [JC] A registry endpoint must be https, with no exception -- localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 included -- because an endpoint receives a credential; a `sparse+` prefix is stripped before the check. userinfo, query and fragment are rejected; an IPv6 endpoint renders with exactly one pair of brackets. One function enforces this for both config load (E197 family) and release binding (E126). Source: crates/callisto-graph/src/registry_endpoint.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/binding.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs. [JC] Package names are validated per ecosystem (cargo, npm, PyPI grammars) before reaching argv or URLs: leading dash, whitespace, control characters, slashes, %, ?, # and out-of-grammar names are rejected; npm workspace names are passed in joined form (--workspace=NAME); tag names reject a leading hyphen; artifact slot components reject . and .. [XC] The orchestration revision is github.sha of the run (assigned exactly once from TRIGGERING_SHA), never the moving tip of main, because attestations are stamped with the run's SHA; the run envelope then requires it to equal every slot's attestation workflow commit. Source: .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml, .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh, crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs. Tests: envelope_rejects_each_cross_field_mismatch. [UR] Release publication is authorized only by a merge: the release path runs on refs/heads/main only, and is_release_pr is true only for exactly one merged managed-branch PR into main from the same repository whose release-source commit is GitHub-verified (signed). Source: .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml, .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh, .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh. Policy self-test mutants (.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh --self-test): verified requirement dropped; verified query dropped.

[UR] No GitHub Environment or approval gate is used on any job; plan runs only when release-candidate says is_release_pr, and execute requires plan success and needs plan, build and release-candidate. [JC] The setup-callisto and setup-callisto-wasm installers verify a downloaded prebuilt asset with gh attestation verify (pinned repo and signer workflow) before extracting only the binary, per a verification input with three modes: require (failure or missing gh aborts, asset never run), fallback (the default: warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io with the version pin kept; for wasm, which has no source install, behaves like require) and skip (no verification, warning, asset used); any other value fails. [JC] A deterministic fault-injection simulator drives the real execute_release and ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting each provider outcome plus every crash-and-fault pair (no randomness, no clock), with every rerun starting from fresh in-memory state, and asserts after each scenario: no duplicate landing, no effect before its prerequisites, a receipt only over landed effects that records exactly the evidence the world holds, convergence within bounded reruns (except a rerun re-issuing an effect a lagging index still reports absent, which only the provider can refuse), and no downstream effect after a permanent conflict. The simulator's invariant checker discriminates: it reports a duplicate landing against a lying provider, an effect preceding its prerequisite, a receipt whose effects never landed, and a receipt whose evidence the world does not hold.
